newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Tension mounts again in riot-torn French Guiana.
newsitem.headline: Tension mounts again in riot-torn French Guiana.

text.p: Riot police returned to the streets of French Guiana late on Wednesday in anticipation of fresh violence after five days of negotiations between local farmers and the French government broke down, witnesses said.
"They (the government) take us for jackassess," farmers leader Christian Epailly told local state-owned television.
Farmers have been at odds with government loan repayment programmes and land title policies in this French overseas territory on the northeast coast of South America.
Late on Tuesday farmers set fire to a government agriculture building causing extensive damage to computers and records, officials said.
On Wednesday, groups of farmers blocked an access road to the French Guiana prefecture for several hours in the capital, Cayenne, with heavy construction equipment.
They broke windows, burned piles of hay and spread manure in front of the building.
There were no immediate reports of injuries.
French Guiana was ravaged by four nights of riots in November by armed gangs of organised youths. It caused one death and millions of dollars of damage to shops and government buildings.
Paris flew in more than 500 paramilitary riot police to patrol the streets of this city of 35,000 in case of fresh violence.

The riots were sparked by a strike of high school students protesting against poor conditions in local schools. They were joined by more radical groups, some of whom favour French Guiana's independence from Paris.
